findings.title: Federated recovery codes are not consumed after successful use
findings.body: After `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().isValid(...)` succeeds, this code fetches the recovery-code credential only to inspect `allCodesUsed()`. It never marks the submitted code as used or removes it. The built-in local recovery-code provider consumes the code during `isValid`, but the new user-storage path delegates validation to the storage provider. The included `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid` does a raw list comparison and returns true without updating the stored data, so the same backup code remains valid and can be replayed, and `allCodesUsed()` never becomes true so the user is never forced to renew codes. Recovery/backup codes must be single-use.

findings.title: Recovery-code credential returned with an ID that does not match persisted federated credential
findings.body: `updateCredential` persists `recoveryCodesModel` with the ID assigned at line 195 (`KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()`). `getCredentials` ignores that persisted model and builds a new `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` via `createFromValues` from the raw JSON, returning a different (or null) credential ID. `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` later calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` when `allCodesUsed()` is true. Because that ID does not identify the stored federated credential, removal fails/no-ops and the used-up recovery-code credential remains in user storage. The provider should preserve the persisted credential ID and update the same model as codes are used.
